body:
Slice #259, "Releasing", round 1: approve. Every Acceptance case exists, runs in CI's scripts job (release.test.sh 27 passed, settings.test.sh 33, reset-db.test.sh 13) or in `check.sh` as the slice names, and tests the script's behaviour through stubbed `docker`, `git` and `curl` rather than a mock of it. I found no blocking defect in `release.sh`.

What I checked beyond the tests: the rollback diff pathspec `:(glob)**/migrations/**` covers `Core/migrations`, `Brain/migrations` and `review/migrations`, the only migration folders at this sha. Postgres is `postgres:18`, not release tagged, so step 4's `up -d --wait postgres` does not recreate it on every release. The backup name grep matches `backup.sh`'s `<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>-<db>.dump.age`. `git checkout` unlinks before it writes, so the running script keeps reading its own inode. Nothing in `compose.yaml` bind mounts a writable path into the clone, so the untracked files check will not trip on the copy's own output. `.release` is ignored. No value is echoed or passed in argv, and the printed restore command passes `-e POSTGRES_PASSWORD` by name only. The runbook's `platform_core invite`, `accounts(id, email)` and `brain import --as` match the code. The deny rules are exactly the three Settled lists.

## Blocking

None.

## Nits

- `scripts/deploy/release.test.sh:1038`: the comment says "Every secret the env file holds is printed by a call", but the docker fake prints none. So `no_secret_is_printed` covers the script's own messages and every fake's argv, which is what Acceptance asks for, but it does not cover the script passing through a command's output unread, which is what the comment claims. Either make the comment match what the fake does or have a fake print a secret.
- `scripts/deploy/release.test.sh:1166`: `the_steps_run_in_order` checks `brain.sh`, `review.sh` and `zz-backup-role.sh` but not `core.sh`, so dropping one of the init scripts from the loop would not be caught for the core. This is minor, since the loop is a glob.
- `infra/hosted/.env.example` (not in the diff), the `BACKUP_AT`/`TZ` comment: "A TZ exported in the shell running compose wins over this file, as every variable does" is no longer true for a release, which unsets every name first. The README says so under "Releasing", but this file is the one the owner reads while filling `.env`. I think the example's comment should change, not the script.
- `infra/hosted/README.md`, "Releasing": "To release an older commit again ... name it" does not say what happens across a migration. I believe the older binary's migrate will refuse a database with migrations it does not know, which fails safely at step 6, but I did not confirm this for all three services. A sentence pointing at the "database is ahead" restore path would save the owner a surprise. Relatedly, releasing a commit from before this pull request checks out a tree with no `scripts/deploy/release.sh` and no `.release` ignore entry, so the next release could not start from the clone until it is checked out to `main` again. This is an edge case, and is worth one line.

## For the owner

None. Every recorded decision is within what Settled and the docs leave open and meets the stricter or more consistent option. Two I checked in particular. Requiring `CORE_SIGNING_KEY` but not the commented optional names is the only workable reading of "every variable `.env.example` names", since requiring `PLATFORM_RELEASE` or `HOSTED_HTTP_BIND` would be wrong. Never tagging `--local` images with a commit sha is the right call given the shared `platform-hosted/<service>` image names.

## Replies

None.
